title: [Epic][IAM-CON] Falcone contracts and ownership
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-CON -->

## Outcome

Freeze observable compatibility and a single writer for each security object.

## Scope

A custom Falcone service; preserve Falcone contracts and enforce tenant/workspace boundaries. See [architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) and [requirements](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/requirements.md).

## Stories

- [ ] IAM-CON-001: Inventory Falcone IAM contracts and consumers
- [ ] IAM-CON-002: Define the identity and authorization ownership boundary
- [ ] IAM-CON-003: Select and qualify the protocol implementation

## Exit criteria

All child acceptance criteria are met, evidence is linked, and the integration/security impact is reviewed. Planning publication does not mark this epic implemented.

title: [IAM-CON-001] Inventory Falcone IAM contracts and consumers
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-CON-001 -->

Parent: IAM-CON

## User story

As a platform maintainer, I want a versioned inventory of identity and permission contracts, so that replacement scope is measurable.

## Description

A versioned inventory of identity and permission contracts.

Phase: P0 · Effort: M

## Requirements

- **FR-CON-001-1**: The system must preserve the approved Falcone IAM API paths, response schemas, errors and tenant/workspace semantics in a versioned contract suite.
- **FR-CON-001-2**: The migration inventory must classify every identity consumer and native Keycloak dependency as retained, adapted or retired.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record current endpoints, issuer/audience assumptions, custom claims, role catalog and all consumers against a pinned Falcone commit.
- [ ] Fixtures exercise positive and negative behavior in both control-plane implementations and the consoles.
- [ ] Separate implemented contracts, source-declared capabilities and unverified deployment assumptions; product owners approve the compatibility list.

## Dependencies

None; discovery can start independently.

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-CON-002] Define the identity and authorization ownership boundary
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-CON-002 -->

Parent: IAM-CON

## User story

As a system architect, I want one authoritative owner per identity, role, resource and quota, so that integrations avoid conflicting writes.

## Description

One authoritative owner per identity, role, resource and quota.

Phase: P0 · Effort: M

## Requirements

- **FR-CON-002-1**: The system must document one authoritative writer and a versioned projection contract for every shared identity and authorization entity.
- **FR-CON-002-2**: The system must consume Falcone plan and quota decisions without maintaining a second independently editable entitlement catalog.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Publish an ownership matrix for users, memberships, roles, resources, credentials, keys, quotas and audit events.
- [ ] Preserve custom role semantics from the Falcone authorization model, including custom: names and subset-of-creator constraints.
- [ ] Define bootstrap ordering so IAM login and authorization do not depend synchronously on workflow or serverless availability.

## Dependencies

IAM-CON-001

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-CON-003] Select and qualify the protocol implementation
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-CON-003 -->

Parent: IAM-CON

## User story

As a security engineer, I want a maintained protocol library behind Falcone interfaces, so that the team can customize the product without inventing authentication protocols.

## Description

A maintained protocol library behind Falcone interfaces.

Phase: P0 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-CON-003-1**: The implementation must use maintained cryptographic and OIDC/OAuth libraries with pinned versions, dependency provenance and an upgrade owner.
- **FR-CON-003-2**: The release process must run the chosen OIDC conformance profile and documented OAuth negative tests against the configured Falcone service.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Prototype the proposed Node.js oidc-provider adapter with PostgreSQL persistence and production key custody; compare Go/Fosite or a Hydra adapter if a mandatory feature fails.
- [ ] Record supported flows, unsupported extensions, license obligations, key-signing integration and measured operational costs in an ADR.
- [ ] Passing library certification must not be represented as certification of Falcone; release requires tests of Falcone configuration and adapters.

## Dependencies

IAM-CON-001

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-IDN-001] Implement principals and scoped memberships
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-IDN-001 -->

Parent: IAM-IDN

## User story

As a tenant administrator, I want stable identities with explicit tenant and workspace memberships, so that users can join multiple workspaces without crossing boundaries.

## Description

Stable identities with explicit tenant and workspace memberships.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-IDN-001-1**: The system must identify principals with immutable IDs and represent tenant/workspace membership separately from profile attributes.
- **FR-IDN-001-2**: Every identity lookup and mutation must enforce its tenant boundary, including when two issuers use the same subject or client identifier.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Uniqueness and foreign-key checks include the relevant tenant scope; tests reuse identical display names across tenants.
- [ ] Legacy identities map by verified issuer and subject, never by email alone.
- [ ] Membership changes use optimistic version checks and cannot delete or demote the final active tenant owner without an approved transfer.

## Dependencies

IAM-CON-002

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-IDN-002] Implement invitations, provisioning and suspension
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-IDN-002 -->

Parent: IAM-IDN

## User story

As a tenant owner, I want idempotent invitation and deprovisioning flows, so that access follows the tenant lifecycle.

## Description

Idempotent invitation and deprovisioning flows.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-IDN-002-1**: The system must support expiring single-use invitations, activation, suspension, reactivation and membership removal through Falcone APIs.
- **FR-IDN-002-2**: Lifecycle mutations must commit an audit record and durable propagation event with their authoritative state change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Invite redemption is tenant-bound and cannot be replayed or claimed through unverified account linking.
- [ ] Repeated provisioning requests with one idempotency key return the original result; conflicting payload reuse fails.
- [ ] Suspension stops new sessions immediately and produces observable downstream revocation jobs; incomplete cleanup is visible and retryable.

## Dependencies

IAM-IDN-001

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-IDN-003] Implement self-service profile and safe account linking
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-IDN-003 -->

Parent: IAM-IDN

## User story

As an end user, I want verified profile updates and account linking, so that I can maintain my account without losing control of it.

## Description

Verified profile updates and account linking.

Phase: P2 · Effort: M

## Requirements

- **FR-IDN-003-1**: The system must require fresh authentication and proof of both identities before linking local and federated accounts.
- **FR-IDN-003-2**: The system must support verified email changes and configurable profile fields without allowing clients to set tenant, role or entitlement claims.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Email normalization and uniqueness policy are explicit per tenant and do not silently merge accounts.
- [ ] Changing an email verifies the new address and notifies the existing address; recovery channel changes require step-up.
- [ ] Unlinking the last usable authentication method fails; an administrator cannot silently impersonate the linked user.

## Dependencies

IAM-IDN-001, IAM-AUT-002

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-AUT-001] Implement local authentication and abuse controls
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-AUT-001 -->

Parent: IAM-AUT

## User story

As an end user, I want a Falcone login flow with secure credential handling, so that I can sign in reliably.

## Description

A Falcone login flow with secure credential handling.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-AUT-001-1**: The system must hash local passwords using a reviewed adaptive password-hashing library and configurable cost policy, never reversible encryption.
- **FR-AUT-001-2**: The system must rate-limit login, signup and recovery attempts by multiple signals and return non-enumerating public failure responses.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Use a measured Argon2id profile unless the approved cryptographic environment requires a reviewed alternative; rehash on successful login when policy changes.
- [ ] Login interactions are CSRF-protected, expire and bind to the correct authorization request; credentials and tokens never enter logs.
- [ ] Distributed abuse tests cover password spraying and limiter-store failure without permitting unbounded hashing work or permanent attacker-controlled lockout.

## Dependencies

IAM-IDN-001, IAM-CON-003

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-AUT-002] Implement passkeys, MFA and step-up
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-AUT-002 -->

Parent: IAM-AUT

## User story

As a security administrator, I want passkeys and enforced MFA for sensitive actions, so that account compromise has a smaller impact.

## Description

Passkeys and enforced MFA for sensitive actions.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-AUT-002-1**: The system must support WebAuthn credentials and TOTP with audited enrollment, removal and recovery-code lifecycle.
- **FR-AUT-002-2**: The system must require policy-defined recent MFA for administrator access and high-risk credential or permission changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] WebAuthn verification checks RP ID, origin, challenge, user verification and credential ownership; challenges are single-use.
- [ ] TOTP secrets are encrypted with managed keys and recovery codes are hashed and single-use; replay and clock-skew rules are tested.
- [ ] Step-up freshness and authentication method are carried in trusted session state; losing a factor cannot bypass the recovery policy.

## Dependencies

IAM-AUT-001, IAM-KEY-001

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-AUT-003] Implement recovery and lifecycle screens
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-AUT-003 -->

Parent: IAM-AUT

## User story

As an end user, I want recovery and account-status flows in the Falcone console, so that I can regain access without weakening authentication.

## Description

Recovery and account-status flows in the Falcone console.

Phase: P2 · Effort: M

## Requirements

- **FR-AUT-003-1**: The system must expose the existing login, signup, pending activation, suspended, expired credentials and password recovery states through Falcone contracts.
- **FR-AUT-003-2**: Password resets must use expiring single-use secrets and revoke affected sessions according to the documented recovery policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recovery does not reveal whether an address exists and cannot downgrade administrator MFA.
- [ ] Email delivery uses a retryable outbox with redacted payload handling and no credential leakage in URLs or logs.
- [ ] Console tests cover stale links, expired sessions, resumed navigation and accessible keyboard-driven login and recovery.

## Dependencies

IAM-AUT-002, IAM-SES-001

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-SES-001] Implement standards-based authorization and token endpoints
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-SES-001 -->

Parent: IAM-SES

## User story

As an application developer, I want OIDC discovery and authorization-code flows, so that Falcone and external clients can authenticate consistently.

## Description

OIDC discovery and authorization-code flows.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-SES-001-1**: The system must provide OIDC discovery, JWKS, authorization, token and user-info endpoints for explicitly configured platform and tenant issuers.
- **FR-SES-001-2**: Public clients must use authorization code with PKCE S256, exact registered redirects and state/nonce validation; implicit and password grants must be disabled.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Clients cannot select another tenant by untrusted headers or arbitrary issuer URLs; issuer metadata and redirect allowlists are validated.
- [ ] Access tokens validate issuer, audience, allowed algorithm, expiry and token purpose; ID tokens are rejected by resource APIs.
- [ ] Authenticated confidential clients and public clients use distinct policies; consent is scoped, revocable and cannot expand requested permissions.

## Dependencies

IAM-CON-003, IAM-IDN-001, IAM-KEY-001

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-SES-002] Implement refresh rotation and session APIs
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-SES-002 -->

Parent: IAM-SES

## User story

As an end user, I want inspectable sessions with safe refresh and logout, so that I can control signed-in devices.

## Description

Inspectable sessions with safe refresh and logout.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-SES-002-1**: The system must rotate refresh tokens atomically, persist only protected token representations and invalidate a token family on confirmed reuse.
- **FR-SES-002-2**: The system must preserve Falcone session refresh/logout behavior and allow authorized users to list and revoke their sessions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Concurrent refresh requests have a documented single-winner or bounded safe retry behavior; no indefinite reuse grace window exists.
- [ ] Session idle and absolute lifetimes are enforced independently; refresh checks current membership, credential version and account status.
- [ ] Console refresh failure clears authenticated state and returns to login; logout distinguishes local client, session and global-account revocation.

## Dependencies

IAM-SES-001

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-SES-003] Implement token status and bounded authorization freshness
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-SES-003 -->

Parent: IAM-SES

## User story

As a resource service owner, I want explicit token-status and authorization freshness semantics, so that local validation does not hide revocation.

## Description

Explicit token-status and authorization freshness semantics.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-SES-003-1**: The system must expose authenticated introspection and revocation interfaces and define a measurable freshness bound for every enforcement surface.
- **FR-SES-003-2**: Authorization decisions must return the effective policy revision and refuse a minimum revision that cannot be satisfied.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] JWT signature verification alone is never documented as immediate revocation; online and offline validation profiles have distinct limits.
- [ ] Protected operations reject expired freshness leases when IAM or projection state is unavailable.
- [ ] Tests revoke a credential, change a role and isolate the event broker, then verify each consumer honors its declared bound.

## Dependencies

IAM-SES-002, IAM-RBAC-002

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-RBAC-001] Implement the canonical role catalog and custom roles
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-RBAC-001 -->

Parent: IAM-RBAC

## User story

As a tenant administrator, I want Falcone roles and bounded custom roles, so that I can delegate only permissions I control.

## Description

Falcone roles and bounded custom roles.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-RBAC-001-1**: The system must preserve the approved platform, tenant and workspace roles and resource/action permission matrix from Falcone internal contracts.
- **FR-RBAC-001-2**: Custom role creation and assignment must enforce namespace, scope, reserved-name and subset-of-delegable-permissions constraints.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests cover platform, tenant and workspace scope plus custom: prefix validation and cross-tenant role collisions.
- [ ] Role edits are versioned and emit effective-permission recalculation events; stale writers receive a conflict.
- [ ] An administrator cannot grant platform privileges or a permission beyond their authorized delegation set, including through nested membership.

## Dependencies

IAM-CON-002, IAM-IDN-001

title: [IAM-RBAC-002] Implement authorization decisions and batch checks
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-RBAC-002 -->

Parent: IAM-RBAC

## User story

As a backend developer, I want one explainable permission-check contract, so that all Falcone APIs enforce the same rules.

## Description

One explainable permission-check contract.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-RBAC-002-1**: The system must evaluate trusted actor, tenant, workspace, action, resource, scopes and delegation context with deny-by-default behavior.
- **FR-RBAC-002-2**: Single and batch authorization APIs must return Falcone decision IDs, effect, reason, matched policies, effective roles and correlation context.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Missing context, cross-tenant resources, insufficient scopes and invalid delegation produce the existing normalized error categories.
- [ ] Resource ownership comes from authoritative service metadata; callers cannot authorize by supplying a forged owner or tenant field.
- [ ] A golden suite verifies role grants intersect with client scopes and delegated authority, explicit denies win, and plan limits never grant access.

## Dependencies

IAM-RBAC-001

## Design reference

title: [IAM-RBAC-003] Implement bounded conditions and data authorization projections
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-RBAC-003 -->

Parent: IAM-RBAC

## User story

As a data service owner, I want versioned authorization projections, so that resource filtering stays consistent with permission checks.

## Description

Versioned authorization projections.

Phase: P2 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-RBAC-003-1**: The system must publish scoped projections for data, function, event and storage consumers with version and delegation context.
- **FR-RBAC-003-2**: Conditional policies must use a bounded approved schema with deterministic evaluation and explicit missing-attribute behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No tenant-supplied code executes inside IAM; policy limits reject recursive or oversized rule sets.
- [ ] List and read queries are filtered before pagination and counts are computed, preventing unauthorized existence disclosure.
- [ ] PostgreSQL RLS and document-store enforcement receive equivalent tenant/workspace scope; a broad API-level allow cannot disable row filtering.

title: [IAM-MAC-001] Implement service accounts and API-key lifecycle
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-MAC-001 -->

Parent: IAM-MAC

## User story

As a workspace administrator, I want scoped service accounts and rotatable API credentials, so that automation does not use human accounts.

## Description

Scoped service accounts and rotatable API credentials.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-MAC-001-1**: The system must create, disable, rotate and revoke service-account credentials with tenant/workspace, scope and audience restrictions.
- **FR-MAC-001-2**: API-key secrets must be shown only at issuance and stored as non-recoverable verifiers with a public identifier for lookup.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Client-credentials tokens use a distinct machine principal type and cannot impersonate a human subject.
- [ ] Rotation supports a bounded overlap policy and revokes the correct credential version even for identically named clients in different tenants.
- [ ] Credential use and failures are auditable without exposing secrets; unknown or deleted credential state is denied.

## Dependencies

IAM-IDN-001, IAM-RBAC-002, IAM-KEY-001

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-MAC-002] Implement scoped delegation for functions and workflows
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-MAC-002 -->

Parent: IAM-MAC

## User story

As a workflow author, I want short-lived delegated capabilities for activities, so that long-running work never stores a broad user token.

## Description

Short-lived delegated capabilities for activities.

Phase: P2 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-MAC-002-1**: Delegated credentials must identify actor and subject, restrict resource audience and intersect all parent scopes and tenant/workspace boundaries.
- **FR-MAC-002-2**: Serverless and workflow execution must renew authorized machine credentials without persisting human refresh tokens in runtime payloads or histories.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Preserve current function invocation signature, audience, body binding and maximum lifetime until a versioned replacement contract is qualified.
- [ ] A workflow paused beyond access-token expiry resumes only after fresh authorization; removed membership cannot be recovered by replaying history.
- [ ] The adapter rejects delegation loops and excessive depth, binds callbacks to execution identity, and tests cancellation and permission loss in current and future runtimes.

## Dependencies

Parent: IAM-KEY

## User story

As a security operator, I want managed key custody and tested rotation, so that token verification remains safe during normal and emergency changes.

## Description

Managed key custody and tested rotation.

## Requirements

- **FR-KEY-001-1**: The system must store signing material and sensitive recoverable secrets using approved OpenBao/KMS-backed protection with least-privilege access.
- **FR-KEY-001-2**: Key rotation must publish new public keys before use, retain required verification overlap and support emergency compromise handling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Select a proven remote-signing or encrypted-key adapter and document private-key exposure in process memory; never claim non-exportability for an exported key.
- [ ] JWKS caches are keyed by trusted issuer, key ID and algorithm; unknown key storms are rate-limited and cannot trigger arbitrary URL fetches.
- [ ] Rotation tests cover mixed replicas, rolling upgrades, expired cache, compromise and recovery; private keys never appear in images, git or logs.

title: [IAM-REV-001] Implement transactional outbox and projection workers
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-REV-001 -->

Parent: IAM-REV

## User story

As an operator, I want durable versioned identity events, so that a broker outage cannot silently lose security changes.

## Description

Durable versioned identity events.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-REV-001-1**: Every security-state mutation must atomically persist its event in an outbox and deliver it with at-least-once semantics.
- **FR-REV-001-2**: Projection consumers must be idempotent, reject obsolete versions and expose applied revision and reconciliation state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Crash tests cover before commit, after commit, after publish and before acknowledgement without event loss or duplicate effects.
- [ ] Tenant-scoped aggregate sequence numbers prevent stale role or credential resurrection after out-of-order delivery.
- [ ] Retries have bounded backoff, dead-letter handling and an audited replay tool; periodic reconciliation repairs missed projections.

## Dependencies

IAM-IDN-001, IAM-RBAC-001

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

- [ ] Measure the proposed 30-second online revocation bound with a healthy network and test stale-lease denial during outages.
- [ ] WebSocket reconnection cannot restore a revoked subscription; DB session cleanup and S3 credential projection are reported independently.
- [ ] A revocation response distinguishes authoritative commit, downstream completion and irreversible already-delivered data or external effects.

<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-OPS-001 -->

Parent: IAM-OPS

## Description

- **FR-OPS-001-1**: The baseline deployment must run with arbitrary non-root UID, dropped capabilities, read-only root filesystem and no privileged or host access.
- **FR-OPS-001-2**: Installation must use ordinary namespaced workloads without requiring a custom operator, CRDs, cluster-admin or a sandbox runtime.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document the prerequisite PostgreSQL, OpenBao, Kafka, TLS, network and backup services and their actual operator-owned permissions.
- [ ] Qualify two supported Kubernetes minors and the administrator-confirmed OpenShift build; a Kubernetes patch number alone is not an OpenShift support matrix.
- [ ] Multiple replicas, readiness/liveness, graceful shutdown, network policies, disruption budgets and migration jobs pass rollout tests.

## Dependencies

IAM-CON-003, IAM-KEY-001

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-OPS-002] Benchmark and define service objectives
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-OPS-002 -->

Parent: IAM-OPS

## User story

As a product owner, I want measured IAM capacity and availability objectives, so that capacity planning matches identity traffic.

## Description

Measured IAM capacity and availability objectives.

Phase: P0 · Effort: M

## Requirements

- **FR-OPS-002-1**: The project must benchmark token issuance, password login, authorization checks, refresh, key lookup and revocation separately.
- **FR-OPS-002-2**: The project must define availability, latency, recovery and freshness objectives with a documented workload, topology and measurement boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Use the provisional objectives in operations.md as hypotheses; record hardware, policy size, cache hit rate, tenant skew and failure mode.
- [ ] Do not equate prior 100k event messages per second or 10k deployed functions with login or token issuance rate.
- [ ] Test noisy-neighbor limits, broker failure and database failover; revise objectives and sizing from results before making an SLA commitment.

## Dependencies

IAM-CON-001

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-OPS-003] Implement recovery, upgrade and on-call procedures
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-OPS-003 -->

Parent: IAM-OPS

## User story

As an SRE, I want tested restoration and upgrades with named owners, so that IAM failures do not lock out the platform indefinitely.

## Description

Tested restoration and upgrades with named owners.

Phase: P2 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-OPS-003-1**: The service must provide tested backup, restore, schema migration and rollback procedures covering identity state, key access and revocation state.
- **FR-OPS-003-2**: Production release must name runtime maintainers, on-call responders, security qualification owners and product decision owners.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Restore from PostgreSQL and managed-key backups in isolation; rotate a recovery epoch or invalidate sessions to prevent restored stale tokens becoming valid.
- [ ] Prove backward-compatible rolling migrations and define the stop point for irreversible schema or credential changes.
- [ ] Run incident exercises for IdP outage, compromised signing key, stolen refresh family and lost database quorum with measured recovery times.

## Dependencies

IAM-OPS-001, IAM-REV-002, IAM-AUD-001

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-MIG-001] Build a migration inventory and dry-run importer
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-MIG-001 -->

Parent: IAM-MIG

## User story

As a migration engineer, I want repeatable identity and client mapping, so that the cutover has measurable coverage.

## Description

Repeatable identity and client mapping.

Phase: P1 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-MIG-001-1**: Migration tooling must dry-run and report users, issuer-subject mappings, memberships, roles, clients, federation and credential portability without modifying production.
- **FR-MIG-001-2**: The importer must be idempotent, tenant-scoped and produce reconciled counts and a report of unsupported or conflicting objects.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Validate actual Keycloak deployment versions and enabled extensions; never assume all declared adapter versions are deployed.
- [ ] Determine password-hash portability by algorithm and parameters; unsupported credentials require a controlled reset or approved bridge, never plaintext export.
- [ ] Classify sessions, MFA secrets, WebAuthn RP IDs and signing keys independently; do not claim seamless portability for all of them.

## Dependencies

IAM-CON-001, IAM-IDN-001, IAM-FED-002

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-MIG-002] Implement dual-issuer shadow checks and tenant canaries
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-MIG-002 -->

Parent: IAM-MIG

## User story

As a rollout owner, I want a reversible staged migration, so that behavior differences are found before all tenants move.

## Description

A reversible staged migration.

Phase: P3 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-MIG-002-1**: Migration mode must explicitly allowlist old and new issuers, audiences and principal mappings without accepting arbitrary token sources.
- **FR-MIG-002-2**: Tenant canaries must compare authorization outcomes and projection completion before switching the authoritative writer.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Shadow checks produce no duplicate grants, user mutations or external side effects; mismatches are classified and approved.
- [ ] Canary gates cover login, refresh, custom roles, federation, S3, DB, events, MCP, workflows and serverless; native Keycloak passthrough usage is inventoried.
- [ ] Rollback reconciles post-cutover membership and credential changes; it is not an unconditional database snapshot restore.

## Dependencies

IAM-MIG-001, IAM-INT-001, IAM-INT-002, IAM-INT-003, IAM-DEV-003

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).

title: [IAM-MIG-003] Retire Keycloak after compatibility and security gates
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-MIG-003 -->

Parent: IAM-MIG

## User story

As a Falcone product owner, I want a controlled retirement checklist, so that the custom service becomes the supported IAM implementation.

## Description

A controlled retirement checklist.

Phase: P3 · Effort: M

## Requirements

- **FR-MIG-003-1**: Keycloak retirement must require signed-off compatibility, security, recovery and operational readiness evidence for every in-use integration.
- **FR-MIG-003-2**: Retirement must revoke obsolete credentials and trust entries, archive required audit evidence and remove approved legacy routes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Observe a defined rollback window and confirm no unsupported client or enterprise connector remains.
- [ ] Explicitly retire or document operator-only /_native/keycloak paths; do not promise raw Keycloak Admin API compatibility.
- [ ] Record owners, runbook locations, residual exceptions and support policy; removing Keycloak is a separate authorized deployment change.

## Dependencies

IAM-MIG-002, IAM-OPS-003

title: [IAM-DEV-001] Publish API schemas, SDK helpers and local fixtures
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-DEV-001 -->

Parent: IAM-DEV

## User story

As an integration developer, I want versioned schemas and local test identities, so that I can build a Falcone integration without production credentials.

## Description

Versioned schemas and local test identities.

Phase: P1 · Effort: M

## Requirements

- **FR-DEV-001-1**: The project must publish OpenAPI and event schemas plus TypeScript and Go integration examples for the approved contracts.
- **FR-DEV-001-2**: Development fixtures must include multiple tenants, machines, custom roles, expired credentials and negative authorization cases.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Examples distinguish end-user tokens, machine credentials and delegated invocation tokens with correct audiences.
- [ ] Local setup uses synthetic data and generated development keys and cannot enable unverified identity mode in production.
- [ ] Schema compatibility checks detect breaking changes and document deprecation periods and adapter version negotiation.

IAM-CON-001, IAM-RBAC-002

title: [IAM-DEV-002] Implement secure build and dependency maintenance
body:

Parent: IAM-DEV

## User story

As a maintainer, I want reproducible builds and dependency checks, so that IAM releases have attributable provenance.

## Description

Reproducible builds and dependency checks.

Phase: P1 · Effort: M

## Requirements

- **FR-DEV-002-1**: Release builds must pin dependencies and publish an SBOM, signed image provenance and migration compatibility notes.
- **FR-DEV-002-2**: The project must define security patch ownership, vulnerability reporting and dependency update qualification.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CI checks secrets, licenses, vulnerable dependencies and container permissions; exceptions have an owner and expiry.
- [ ] Protocol-library upgrades rerun the configured conformance and regression suites.
- [ ] Select an owner-approved repository license before redistributing third-party code; research references do not authorize copying proprietary extensions.

title: [IAM-DEV-003] Qualify isolation, protocol security and failure behavior
body:
<!-- falcone-iam:IAM-DEV-003 -->

Parent: IAM-DEV

## User story

As a security reviewer, I want adversarial and failure-injection evidence, so that Keycloak is replaced only after the new service proves its boundaries.

## Description

Adversarial and failure-injection evidence.

Phase: P2 · Effort: L

## Requirements

- **FR-DEV-003-1**: A release candidate must pass tenant-isolation, protocol-negative, credential-replay and recovery tests against all enabled integration profiles.
- **FR-DEV-003-2**: Production cutover must require independent security review of authentication, authorization, key custody and deployment configuration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Threat tests cover confused deputy, forged context, OAuth mix-up, CSRF, SSRF, privilege escalation, stale grants and refresh races.
- [ ] Fault tests cover replica crashes, broker partitions, delayed/out-of-order events, DB restore and key rotation with declared fail-closed behavior.
- [ ] Document residual findings, remediation owners and approved exceptions; ordinary containers are not represented as a security sandbox for hostile tenant code.

## Dependencies

IAM-SES-003, IAM-AUT-002, IAM-MAC-002, IAM-RBAC-003, IAM-OPS-003, IAM-DEV-002

## Design reference

[Architecture](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) · [Integration matrix](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/integration-matrix.md) · [Security](https://github.com/gntik-ai/falcone-iam/blob/main/docs/security.md).
